user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a private REST API Gateway in a VPC, intended to ingest commands from an App Runner service, using the application name "shopify" and environment "development" as defaults. The template must first deploy a VPC endpoint of type Interface for the execute-api service, with private DNS enabled, attached to the VPC, private subnets (app-private-subnet-a and app-private-subnet-b), and security group (app-sg) imported from a separate stack using the naming convention `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:vpc`, `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:app-private-subnet-a`, etc. The API Gateway itself must be configured as a private endpoint, referencing that VPC endpoint, with a resource policy that allows invoke from any principal but denies invoke unless the request originates from the specific VPC endpoint. It must include a Cognito user pool authorizer of type COGNITO_USER_POOLS, using the imported Cognito user pool ARN (exported as `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:cognito-userpool-arn`), with the identity source set to the Authorization header. A proxy resource with path `{proxy+}` should be created, and a method of ANY HTTP method must be integrated as AWS_PROXY, forwarding requests to a Lambda function whose ARN is imported from `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:lambda-api-function-arn`, using POST as the integration HTTP method. An IAM role named "ApiGatewayLogPublishingRole" must be created with the AmazonAPIGatewayPushToCloudWatchLogs managed policy, allowing the API Gateway service to assume it, and this role must be associated via an AWS::ApiGateway::Account resource. A deployment must be created, depending on the method, and a stage named after the Environment parameter (e.g., "development") must be configured with caching disabled, detailed logging at INFO level, metrics enabled, data trace enabled, throttling rate limit of 10000 requests per second and burst limit of 5000, and an access log setting that writes to a CloudWatch log group named `/${AppName}/apigateway/access-log` with a retention of 7 days, using a JSON format that captures requestId, source IP, caller, user, requestTime, eventType, routeKey, status, and connectionId. Finally, a Lambda permission must grant the API Gateway service invoke access on the imported Lambda function, scoped to the API's resource path. The template should output the service endpoint URL as `https://${ApiGatewayRestApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}` and export it as `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:api-gateway-endpoint`.

The EventBridge rule should be enabled and match `aws.ec2` source, detail-type `EC2 Instance State-change Notification`, with state `running`. A Lambda permission must allow events.amazonaws.com to invoke the function. The template should output the Lambda function name and the EventBridge rule name.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a regional Web Application Firewall (WAF) for protecting an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, designed for the RoboSystems service across prod and staging environments. The template should accept the ARN of the API ALB to protect, a configurable rate limit per IP address with a default of 3000 requests per 5-minute window, and an optional toggle for geographic blocking that, when enabled, blocks all traffic except from the United States and Canada. It must also include an optional toggle for the AWS Managed Core Rule Set, with several specific rules excluded to prevent false positives with browser traffic, such as NoUserAgent_HEADER, UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER, SizeRestrictions_BODY, SizeRestrictions_QUERYSTRING, GenericRFI_BODY, GenericRFI_QUERYARGUMENTS, GenericRFI_URIPATH, RestrictedExtensions_URIPATH, RestrictedExtensions_QUERYARGUMENTS, EC2MetaDataSSRF_BODY, and EC2MetaDataSSRF_QUERYARGUMENTS. The WAF must include a default Allow action with six priority-ordered rules: first, an IP set allowlist using a comma-delimited list of IPs or CIDRs (defaulting to 0.0.0.0/32) that bypasses all other rules; second, the rate-based blocking rule returning a 429 status code with a JSON body stating "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."; third, a combined rule blocking SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks on query arguments, the request body (with oversize handling set to CONTINUE), and the URI path, returning a 403 status code with a JSON body stating "Request blocked due to security rules."; fourth, a size restriction rule blocking request bodies over 8MB (with oversize handling set to CONTINUE) and headers over 8KB, returning a 413 status code with a JSON body stating "Request payload too large."; fifth, the optional geographic blocking rule returning a 403 status code with a JSON body stating "Access denied from your location."; and sixth, the optional AWS managed rule set with a None override action. The template must create an IP set resource for the allowlist, the Web ACL with custom response bodies for each blocking scenario, and a WebACLAssociation resource that conditionally associates the WAF with the provided ALB ARN only if the ARN is not empty. All resources must be tagged with Name, Environment, Service (defaulting to RoboSystems), Component (defaulting to WAF), and CreatedBy set to CloudFormation. The outputs should export the Web ACL ID, Web ACL ARN, and the allowed IP set ARN, along with an estimated monthly cost string that shows $6-7 when managed rules are enabled and $5.60-6.20 when they are not.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an RDS Proxy for an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, intended to manage database connections securely and efficiently for a serverless application. The template should accept parameters for the application name, defaulting to "shopify", and the proxy name, defaulting to "aurora-cluster". It must create an IAM role named "ProxyDbSecretsAccessRole" that allows the RDS service to assume it, and attach a custom managed policy called "DbSecretsManagerManagedPolicy" that grants the secretsmanager:GetSecretValue action on a secret imported from another stack using the format "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-secrets". Two security groups are required: one named "AuroraProxySecurityGroup" and another named "LambdaApiSecurityGroup", both associated with a VPC imported via the key "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:vpc", with appropriate tags for the application name. An ingress rule must allow TCP traffic on port 5432 from the Lambda API security group to the Aurora proxy security group. The RDS Proxy resource itself should be named using the proxy parameter, use the POSTGRESQL engine family, enable debug logging, set an idle client timeout of 120 seconds, require TLS, and reference the IAM role ARN. Its authentication must use the SECRETS scheme with the same imported secret ARN and require IAM authentication. The proxy must be deployed across two private subnets imported as "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-private-subnet-a" and "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-private-subnet-b", and include both the Aurora proxy security group and an imported database security group from the key "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-sg". A default target group for the proxy must associate it with the Aurora cluster imported via "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-cluster", and configure connection pooling with MaxConnectionsPercent set to 100, MaxIdleConnectionsPercent set to 50, and ConnectionBorrowTimeout set to 120 seconds. Finally, the template should export the proxy endpoint, proxy ARN, Aurora proxy security group ID, and Lambda API security group ID using the naming convention "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-proxy-endpoint", "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-proxy-arn", "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-proxy-sg", and "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:lambda-api-sg" respectively.

It must also create an ECS service that imports the cluster name, Fargate container security group, and both public subnets from the parent stack, enables public IP assignment, uses a deployment configuration with a maximum of 200 percent and minimum healthy percent of 75, and attaches to a target group. Finally, it must create a listener rule that forwards traffic from the imported public listener to the target group based on the specified path pattern and priority. user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a highly available, internet-facing web application deployment using an Application Load Balancer, an Auto Scaling group, and EC2 instances running Amazon Linux 2, all designed to support weighted DNS routing for blue/green or canary deployments. The template must accept parameters for the instance type (defaulting to t2.micro with options like t2.small, t2.medium, t3.micro, t3.small, t3.medium), the environment tag (dev, qa, or prod, defaulting to dev), the AppName tag (defaulting to "AWS CloudFormation Workshop - example app"), the Name tag (defaulting to "AWS CloudFormation Workshop"), and the page text content which can be "Hello world!", "Blue", or "Green" (defaulting to "Hello world!"). The AMI should be dynamically resolved using the SSM parameter /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/amzn2-ami-hvm-x86_64-gp2. The template must import the VPC ID, public subnet IDs, and private subnet IDs from a network stack whose name is parameterized (defaulting to "cloudformation-workshop-dev-base-network"), and import the hosted zone ID and name from a hosted zone stack (defaulting to "cloudformation-workshop-dev-hosted-zone"), as well as security group IDs for both the load balancer and the application instances from a security group stack (defaulting to "cloudformation-workshop-dev-security-groups"). The load balancer should be internet-facing, of type application, using IPv4, and be placed in two public subnets. A listener on port 80 HTTP must forward traffic to a target group that uses instance type targets on port 80 HTTP, with health checks every 30 seconds, a 5-second timeout, 5 healthy thresholds, 2 unhealthy thresholds, and a 200 HTTP code matcher. The Auto Scaling group should have a desired capacity of 2, a minimum of 2, and a maximum of 4, using a launch template that references the latest Amazon Linux 2 AMI and the chosen instance type, and it must be placed in two private subnets. The launch template must include user data that runs cfn-init to install and configure the Apache httpd service, deploy a simple index.html file containing the page text content, set up the cfn-hup daemon to automatically re-run cfn-init on stack updates, and then signal success to the Auto Scaling group with a 15-minute timeout. The Auto Scaling group must use a rolling update policy with a batch size of 1, keeping at least 2 instances in service, and waiting for resource signals with a 15-minute pause time. A Route 53 A record set with an alias target pointing to the load balancer's DNS name and hosted zone ID must be created in the imported hosted zone, with a configurable weight (defaulting to 0, range 0-255) and a set identifier that includes the AppName and stack name. All taggable resources must be tagged with Name, AppName, and Env tags. The template should output the application URL as http:// followed by the load balancer's DNS name.

The template should generate four secrets in AWS Secrets Manager: a JWT signing secret named wealthwise/jwt-secret with a 64-character alphanumeric password excluding punctuation, a JWT refresh token signing secret named wealthwise/jwt-refresh-secret with the same generation rules, a MongoDB/DocumentDB connection string secret named wealthwise/mongodb-uri with the literal placeholder value 'REPLACE_WITH_DOCUMENTDB_CONNECTION_STRING', and a NextAuth.js session encryption secret named wealthwise/nextauth-secret also generated with a 64-character alphanumeric string. All secrets must be tagged with the environment name parameter (defaulting to production). Additionally, the template must create an ECS task execution role named with the environment prefix and suffix -wealthwise-ecs-execution, which trusts the ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com service principal, attaches the AWS managed policy AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy, and includes a custom inline policy granting secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on all four secrets. A separate ECS task role named with the environment prefix and suffix -wealthwise-ecs-task, also trusting ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com, must include an inline policy allowing ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel, ssmmessages:CreateDataChannel, ssmmessages:OpenControlChannel, and ssmmessages:OpenDataChannel on all resources to support ECS Exec. The template should output the ARN of each secret and export the execution role ARN and task role ARN using the environment name as a prefix for the export names.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a DynamoDB table for storing book metadata, designed to support efficient querying by category, title, and language. The table should use a composite primary key with Category as the hash key and Title as the range key, both as string attributes. We need a local secondary index named LanguageIndex that uses Category as the hash key and Language as the range key with a KEYS_ONLY projection, allowing us to query books within a category by language. Additionally, we need a global secondary index named TitleIndex that uses Title as the hash key with a KEYS_ONLY projection, enabling lookups by book title across all categories. The table must have point-in-time recovery enabled for data protection. Provisioned throughput should be configurable through parameters, with read capacity units defaulting to 5 and write capacity units defaulting to 10, both constrained between 5 and 10000. The template should output the name of the created DynamoDB table for reference in other stacks or applications.

cfn_description: Plot Palette - Authentication Stack with Cognito User Pool
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure authentication stack for a web application called Plot Palette, using Amazon Cognito to manage user sign-up, sign-in, and account recovery, with the stack being parameterized by an environment name (dev, test, or prod) that defaults to dev. The template must provision a Cognito User Pool named plot-palette-users-{environment} that allows users to sign in with their email address as their username (case-insensitive), automatically verifies email addresses upon registration, and enforces a strict password policy requiring a minimum length of 12 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one symbol, with temporary passwords expiring after 7 days. Multi-factor authentication must be optional but enabled for software token MFA, and account recovery should be handled solely through verified email with a priority of 1. The email verification subject line must be "Verify your Plot Palette account" and the message body must contain the placeholder {####} for the verification code. Admin user creation should not be restricted, and the user pool schema must include the following attributes: email (required, immutable, string), name (optional, mutable, string), a custom attribute called user_role (mutable, string with a minimum length of 1 and maximum of 50), and a custom attribute called organization (mutable, string with a minimum length of 1 and maximum of 100). The user pool must be tagged with Name, Environment, and ManagedBy tags. Additionally, the template must create a web client for the user pool named plot-palette-web-client that does not generate a client secret, supports explicit authentication flows including ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH, ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH, and ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH, and has the PreventUserExistenceErrors setting enabled for security. Token validity must be set to 60 minutes for ID and access tokens, and 30 days for refresh tokens, with appropriate units. The client should read and write the email, email_verified, name, custom:user_role, and custom:organization attributes, and must allow OAuth flows of code and implicit with scopes for email, openid, and profile, with the OAuth flows enabled for the client. Callback URLs must include http://localhost:5173 and http://localhost:3000, and logout URLs must also include those same two localhost addresses, with the only supported identity provider being COGNITO. Finally, the stack must export the User Pool ID, User Pool ARN, User Pool Client ID, and User Pool Provider URL (for JWT issuer) using the stack name as a prefix for the export names.

cfn_description: Route 53 Application Recovery Controller (us-east-1)
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates the foundational infrastructure for an AWS Route 53 Application Recovery Controller setup in the us-east-1 region, designed to support cross-region application failover between us-east-1 and us-west-2. The template must provision a Route 53 Recovery Control cluster named AppFailover-Cluster, along with a control panel named AppFailover-ControlPanel that is associated with this cluster. Two routing controls must be created within this control panel: one named AppFailover-us-east-1 and another named AppFailover-us-west-2, both linked to the same cluster and control panel. To facilitate integration with automation and operational tooling, the template must also create three SSM parameters: one named /app-failover/arc-cluster storing the cluster reference, one named /app-failover/arc-control-us-east-1 storing the reference to the first routing control, and one named /app-failover/arc-control-us-west-2 storing the reference to the second routing control. Additionally, the template must export the cluster ARN and both routing control ARNs as stack outputs with the export names app-failover-arc-cluster, app-failover-arc-control-us-east-1, and app-failover-arc-control-us-west-2 respectively, so that other stacks and external systems can reference these resources for failover orchestration and health check routing.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of CloudWatch Logs Insights queries and a corresponding CloudWatch dashboard for monitoring AWS Client VPN usage, covering AD/SAML, Mutual Auth, and Mixed Auth authentication methods. The template should accept two parameters: a Folder name (defaulting to "aws-client-vpn") to organize the queries, and a ClientVPNLogGroup name (defaulting to "aws/aws-client-vpn/prod") specifying the log group to query. It must create twelve CloudWatch Logs QueryDefinition resources: one for total usage per Client VPN endpoint (aggregating connection count, ingress/egress MB, connection hours, and distinct users), three for AD/SAML auth (total usage report, distinct users connection duration, distinct users list, and users connection duration), three for Mutual Auth (total usage report, users duration, distinct users, and distinct users connection duration), and three for Mixed Auth (total usage report, distinct users connection duration, distinct users, and users connection duration). Additionally, it should create a CloudWatch Dashboard named with the region prefix "AWS-ClientVPN-Usage-Dashboard" containing twelve log table widgets arranged vertically, each displaying the results of the corresponding query against the specified log group. The dashboard body must be constructed using Fn::Sub to inject the log group name and region. Finally, the template should output two URLs: one for the CloudWatch Logs Insights console and one for the created dashboard, both using the region from the stack.

cfn_description: Route 53 DNS with ARC-controlled health checks
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route 53 DNS failover architecture using AWS Resilience Hub (ARC) controlled health checks for a multi-region API deployment. The template should accept a domain name parameter with a default of api-failover-test.example.com, and create a public hosted zone for that domain. It must define two Route 53 health checks of type RECOVERY_CONTROL, each referencing an ARC routing control ARN stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for us-east-1 under the path /app-failover/arc-control-us-east-1, and one for us-west-2 under /app-failover/arc-control-us-west-2. The template should then create two DNS A records with failover routing: a primary record for us-east-1 and a secondary record for us-west-2, each associated with its respective health check. Both records must be aliases to API Gateway endpoints, using the hosted zone IDs Z1UJRXOUMOOFQ8 for us-east-1 and Z2OJLYMUO9EFXC for us-west-2, with the actual DNS names retrieved from SSM parameters /app-failover/api-endpoint-us-east-1 and /app-failover/api-endpoint-us-west-2 respectively, and with EvaluateTargetHealth set to false. Finally, the template should output the hosted zone ID, the domain name, and a comma-separated list of name servers from the hosted zone to be used for registrar delegation.

cfn_description: Shared resources required by all Amazon EKS Quick Start stacks in this account (qs-1r0qgtn7j).
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates the shared IAM roles and instance profiles required by all Amazon EKS Quick Start stacks in an AWS account, designed to support the deployment and management of EKS clusters, node groups, Fargate profiles, and associated networking resources. The template must create Lambda execution roles for various operational tasks, including a CopyZipsRole that allows Lambda to read objects from any S3 bucket, a GenerateClusterNameRole for cluster naming logic, a ResourceReaderRole with ReadOnlyAccess, a CreateVpcRoleRole that can create and attach policies to a role named CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC, a DeleteBucketContentsRole for cleanup operations, and a CloudFormationVPCRoleCreationRole with similar VPC role creation permissions. The template must also include a ControlPlaneRole for the EKS control plane that assumes the AmazonEKSClusterPolicy, AmazonEKSServicePolicy, and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController managed policies plus EC2 describe permissions, a CleanupLoadBalancersRole with permissions to describe and delete application, network, and classic load balancers along with associated network interfaces and security groups, a CleanupSecurityGroupDependenciesRole for removing security group dependencies, a CleanupLambdasRole that can list and delete Lambda functions, a GetCallerArnRole with CloudFormation stack describe and CloudTrail lookup permissions, a RegisterTypeRole for registering CloudFormation resource types with permissions for STS, CloudFormation type registration, IAM role and policy management, S3 object reads, and SSM parameter operations, a NodeSGRole with EKS DescribeNodeGroup permissions, a FargateExecutionRole that can be assumed by eks-fargate-pods.amazonaws.com with the AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy, a FargateProfileRole for creating and managing Fargate profiles with EC2 subnet describe and IAM pass role permissions, and a QuickStartParameterResolverRole with SSM parameter read access restricted to the /quickstart/amazon-eks/ path. The template must also create two EC2 instance profiles, one for unmanaged node groups and one for managed node groups, each referencing corresponding IAM roles that can be assumed by EC2 instances and include the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy, and AmazonElasticContainerRegistryPublicReadOnly managed policies, with the public ECR policy only included when the partition is aws, plus a custom inline policy allowing cloudformation:SignalResource. All Lambda roles must assume the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole managed policy, and all roles must be named with the eks-quickstart prefix as specified. The template must use a condition to check if the AWS partition is aws for the conditional inclusion of the public ECR policy, and all IAM policies should follow least-privilege principles with resource-level restrictions where appropriate, such as limiting S3 get object permissions to any bucket, restricting IAM role creation to the specific CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC role, and scoping SSM parameter access to the quickstart path.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a serverless solution to automatically start and stop EC2 instances across all AWS regions on a recurring schedule, using a single Lambda function triggered by two separate EventBridge rules. The solution should include an IAM role for the Lambda function with permissions to describe regions, describe instances, and start or stop instances in any region, as well as permissions to create CloudWatch log groups and streams and put log events. The Lambda function itself must be written in Python 3.9 with a 60-second timeout, and it should read an environment variable named INSTANCE_IDS_TO_IGNORE_STOP that accepts a string representing a list of instance IDs to exclude from the stop action, with a default value of "['instance-id']". The function should be triggered by a stop rule using a cron expression that defaults to "cron(30 14 ? * FRI *)" and a start rule using a cron expression that defaults to "cron(30 2 ? * MON *)", both enabled by default. Each rule must have a corresponding Lambda permission resource that allows the EventBridge service to invoke the function using the rule’s ARN as the source. The template should accept the cron expressions and the instance ID ignore list as parameters, with the instance ID parameter validated by an allowed pattern that matches a Python list syntax. The Lambda function code should be provided inline and must include logic to determine whether the triggering rule name contains "ScheduledEC2StopRule" or "ScheduledEC2StartRule" to decide whether to stop or start instances, and it should force-stop instances when stopping.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider and a corresponding IAM role to allow GitHub Actions workflows in the PRX organization to securely deploy and manage AWS resources, along with a set of managed policies that grant the role specific, least-privilege permissions for common DevOps tasks. The template must first create an IAM OIDC provider representing GitHub as a trusted identity provider, configured with the URL https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, the client ID sts.amazonaws.com, and the two required thumbprints 6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1 and 1c58a3a8518e8759bf075b76b750d4f2df264fcd. It should then create an IAM role named PRX-GHA-AccessRole with a trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity action from the federated OIDC provider, but only when the audience is sts.amazonaws.com and the subject claim matches the pattern repo:PRX/*:*. This role must be tagged with the keys prx:meta:tagging-version set to 2021-04-07, prx:cloudformation:stack-name, prx:cloudformation:stack-id, prx:ops:environment set to Production, and prx:dev:application set to DevOps. The role should be attached to eight separate managed policies, each with a specific purpose: a CloudFormationStackUpdatePolicy that allows all CloudFormation actions but explicitly denies DeleteStack and DeleteStackSet; an AwsSamS3AccessPolicy that allows s3:Get*, s3:List*, and s3:PutObject on the resource arn:aws:s3:::aws-sam-cli-managed-default-samclisourcebucket*/*; a CodePipelineStartExecutionPolicy that allows codepipeline:StartPipelineExecution on all pipelines; a SesMailSendPolicy that allows ses:SendEmail on all resources; a PassCloudFormationRolePolicy that allows iam:PassRole specifically on the role ARN matching arn:aws:iam::*:role/PRX-GHA-ServiceRoleForCloudFormation; an EcrPublicPushPolicy that allows all necessary actions for pushing Docker images to public ECR repositories including ecr-public:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, CompleteLayerUpload, GetAuthorizationToken, InitiateLayerUpload, PutImage, TagResource, UploadLayerPart, and sts:GetServiceBearerToken; a PrivateEcrPushPolicy that allows the equivalent private ECR actions (ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, CompleteLayerUpload, GetAuthorizationToken, InitiateLayerUpload, PutImage, TagResource, UploadLayerPart, and sts:GetServiceBearerToken); an SsmParameterPutPolicy that allows ssm:PutParameter on resources matching arn:aws:ssm:*:*:parameter/*/pkg/docker-image-tag; and an AssumeRolePolicy that allows sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession on any role, but only when the target role has a resource tag with the key PRX-GHA-AccessRole and the value AssumeRole.

cfn_description: Cloudformation Template to create a VPC with public and private subnets in 3 AZs
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a highly available VPC infrastructure spanning three Availability Zones, designed to support workloads requiring both public-facing and private resources with outbound internet access. The VPC should use a CIDR block of 10.${ClassB}.0.0/16 where ClassB is a user-provided parameter representing the second octet, defaulting to 0 and constrained to the range 0-255, with DNS support and hostname resolution enabled. The template must provision six subnets total—one public and one private in each of the three Availability Zones—with public subnets using /20 CIDR blocks starting at 10.${ClassB}.0.0/20, 10.${ClassB}.32.0/20, and 10.${ClassB}.64.0/20, and private subnets using 10.${ClassB}.16.0/20, 10.${ClassB}.48.0/20, and 10.${ClassB}.80.0/20, with public subnets configured to auto-assign public IPs. An Internet Gateway must be attached to the VPC with a default route of 0.0.0.0/0 in the public route table, while each private subnet requires its own dedicated route table with a 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing to a NAT Gateway deployed in the corresponding public subnet of the same Availability Zone, with each NAT Gateway backed by an Elastic IP. The template must include separate network ACLs for public and private subnets, with the public NACL allowing all inbound and outbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 and the private NACL also allowing all traffic, and these NACLs must be associated with their respective subnets. An S3 VPC Endpoint must be created with a policy allowing all actions and resources, associated with all three private route tables, using the service name format com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3. All resources must be properly tagged with descriptive names incorporating the VPC CIDR and Availability Zone identifiers, and the template must export comprehensive outputs including the VPC ID, CIDR block, the three Availability Zone names, lists of public and private subnet IDs, the public route table ID, the three private route table IDs, individual subnet IDs for each Availability Zone, the S3 VPC Endpoint ID, the stack name, and a template identifier of VPC-3AZs, with all exports using the stack name as a prefix for cross-stack referencing.

cfn_description: StackSet IAM roles
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates the IAM roles required to enable AWS CloudFormation StackSets to manage resources across multiple AWS accounts. The template must provision an IAM role named "AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole" that is assumable by the AWS CloudFormation service principal, allowing it to perform stack set administration tasks. This administrator role must include an inline policy that grants the sts:AssumeRole permission specifically targeting the execution role ARN pattern "arn:aws:iam::*:role/AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole", enabling it to assume corresponding execution roles in any target account. The trust policy for the administrator role must restrict the principal to the cloudformation.amazonaws.com service, ensuring only CloudFormation can assume this role. The primary resource should be a single APS Workspace with an alias dynamically constructed from the project name, 'prometheus', and the environment, tagged with Environment, Service, Component, and a CreatedBy tag set to 'CloudFormation'. The outputs need to export the workspace ARN, workspace ID, the Prometheus endpoint, and a remote write endpoint constructed by appending '/api/v1/remote_write' to the workspace ARN, along with the environment value, all with export names prefixed by the stack name. This role must be attached to a customer-managed IAM policy that grants permissions for mobile analytics event publishing, Cognito Sync operations, SES email sending, Transcribe streaming transcription via WebSocket, Comprehend dominant language detection, and Translate text translation, all with resource-level wildcard access. The identity pool role attachment must map the unauthenticated role to the identity pool so that guest users automatically receive these permissions. The template should output the identity pool ID as a stack output for downstream consumption. The identity pool must be created with unauthenticated identities enabled, and the IAM role's trust policy must use the federated principal for cognito-identity.amazonaws.com with the audience condition matching the identity pool ID and the unauthenticated role condition using the ForAnyValue:StringLike operator. The policy should be named appropriately and attached to the unauthenticated role. The template should also include a conditional CDK metadata resource that only deploys in supported commercial and China regions, listing all the standard AWS regions where this metadata is available.

The API must use a Lambda data source pointing to the created function, and use a single AppSync JavaScript function (runtime APPSYNC_JS 1.0.0) as a pipeline resolver for both the query and mutation, which invokes the Lambda with the field name and arguments. The template should output the GraphQL endpoint URL and the API key value. The Lambda handler should be index.handler and the code should be inline, containing the logic described.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a flexible, multi-tier VPC network environment capable of supporting 1, 2, or 3 tiers across 1, 2, or 3 Availability Zones, designed to be reused by multiple projects with different isolation requirements. The solution must accept a VPC name (defaulting to "dev"), a business scope (defaulting to "example"), and a system identifier (defaulting to "infra") to qualify all resource names, along with a VPC CIDR block defaulting to 10.1.0.0/20. The template should allow the user to specify whether to create an Internet Gateway (default true), whether to create NAT Gateways (default true), and whether to use a single NAT Gateway for all AZs or one per AZ (default true, meaning a single NAT gateway). There will be three optional tiers: Tier 1 (default name "public", enabled by default), Tier 2 (default name "private", enabled by default), and Tier 3 (default name "restricted", disabled by default). Each tier should have CIDR parameters for up to 3 subnets, with default CIDRs of 10.1.0.0/24, 10.1.1.0/24, and 10.1.2.0/24 for Tier 1, 10.1.3.0/24 through 10.1.5.0/24 for Tier 2, and 10.1.6.0/24 through 10.1.8.0/24 for Tier 3, with the caveat that only subnets matching the selected number of AZs are actually created. The template must conditionally create an Internet Gateway and attach it to the VPC, create Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways in Tier 1 subnets (either one or all based on the single NAT flag), and create route tables with default routes to the Internet Gateway for Tier 1 and to the appropriate NAT Gateway for Tier 2 and Tier 3. Additionally, VPC Flow Logs must be enabled capturing all traffic, sending to a CloudWatch Logs group with a 1-day retention, and the log delivery role must include the string "svc-flow-logs" in its name, be placed under a path like "/example/infra/", and must have a set of least-privilege permissions allowing only PutLogEvents, CreateLogGroup, CreateLogStream, DescribeLogGroups, and DescribeLogStreams on log groups matching the pattern "/infra/dev/flowlogs". An optional IAM Permissions Boundary ARN can be provided to attach to the flow logs role. The outputs must export the VPC ID and each created subnet ID for all tiers, using export names in the format "StackName::tiername-subnet-id-N" such as "myStack::public-subnet-id-1". The entire solution must work without requiring any hardcoded AMI IDs or external URLs.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of security groups and ingress rules for a video streaming application, importing the VPC ID from an existing stack named 'video-streaming-vpc' (configurable via a parameter). The template should define a Redis security group that allows all traffic from both the Origin and Server container security groups, a Server load balancer security group that opens TCP port 1935 to the internet (with port 443 commented out), and a Server container security group that opens TCP ports 1935 and 8000 to the internet, plus allows all traffic from the Server load balancer, Proxy container, Origin container, and itself (for inter-process communication). For the Origin tier, create an Origin load balancer security group that opens TCP ports 80 and 443 to the internet, and an Origin container security group that allows TCP port 80 only from the Origin load balancer. For the Proxy tier, create a Proxy container security group that opens TCP ports 1935, 3000, 8080, 80, and 443 to the internet. All security groups must be placed in the imported VPC, and the template should export each security group’s ID with names like RedisSecurityGroup, ServerLoadBalancerSecurityGroup, OriginLoadBalancerSecurityGroup, OriginContainerSecurityGroup, ProxyContainerSecurityGroup, and ServerContainerSecurityGroup, using the stack name as a prefix.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a custom resource to perform arithmetic calculations using a Lambda function, intended for demonstrating custom resource success and failure handling. The template must include four parameters: a string parameter named DoYouWantToSucceed with default value "true" and allowed values "true" and "false" to control whether the custom resource succeeds or intentionally fails; a number parameter named FirstNumber with default 2; a number parameter named SecondNumber with default 2; and a string parameter named Operator with default "*" and allowed values "+", "-", "*", "/" to select the arithmetic operation. The core resources should be an AWS Lambda function named CustomResourceLambda using Python 3.11 runtime, 128 MB memory, and a 1-second timeout, with inline code that handles CloudFormation custom resource events, performs the chosen operation on the two numbers, and returns the result via cfnresponse; an IAM role named CustomResourceRole that allows the Lambda service to assume it; an IAM policy named CustomResourcePolicy granting permissions for logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, and logs:PutLogEvents on all resources, attached to the role; and a custom resource of type Custom::helper named HelperCustomResource that depends on the policy and passes the ServiceToken as the Lambda function ARN along with the parameter values for doYouWantToSucceed, firstNumber, secondNumber, and operator. Finally, the template must output the result of the calculation using the Fn::GetAtt intrinsic function on the custom resource's result attribute.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates two randomly generated secrets in AWS Secrets Manager for disaster recovery preparation, with replication from a primary region to a secondary region, where the secondary region is specified by a parameter defaulting to us-west-2, and the project name parameter defaults to "r24-sec324-protip5". One secret, named with a stack name prefix "-PrimarySecretB", must be encrypted at rest using a customer-managed multi-region KMS key with automatic key rotation, a key policy that allows the account's Admin role full KMS administration, allows any principal in the account to perform Decrypt and GenerateDataKey via the secretsmanager service (with the kms:CallerAccount condition and kms:ViaService restricted to secretsmanager in the primary region), and allows the root user to describe, get, list, and revoke grants on the key; the key should also have an alias like "alias/{stackname}-PrimarySecretB". The secret itself should have a generated password of length 12, excluding characters like backslash, double quote, at sign, and space (as defined by the ExcludeCharacters parameter default), a secret string template with username "loginB", and it must be replicated to the specified replica region. The second secret, named with "-PrimarySecretC", must be encrypted using the default AWS managed key for Secrets Manager (alias/aws/secretsmanager), with the same password generation settings but a username of "UserDB", and also replicated to the same replica region. The template should output the ARNs of both secrets and the ARN of the customer-managed KMS key.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates the necessary IAM infrastructure for an EC2 instance to securely download application artifacts from an S3 bucket, specifically for deploying the Agilefant project management tool. The template should define an IAM role that EC2 instances can assume via the EC2 service principal, along with a corresponding instance profile that can be attached to EC2 instances. The role must have a least-privilege policy that grants permissions to list buckets, get bucket location, and get objects, but only for the S3 bucket named "cfnstore" and specifically for objects within a path that corresponds to a configurable bucket name parameter, which defaults to "agilefant" (so the allowed object ARN should be arn:aws:s3:::cfnstore/agilefant/*). The template should accept a parameter for this bucket name, and the policy should be attached to the role. The template must output both the instance profile name and the IAM role name so they can be referenced by other stacks or used during EC2 launch configuration. The overall purpose is to enable an EC2 instance to download the Agilefant application files from the designated S3 location using temporary credentials from the instance profile.

The role must include a single inline policy named "ResourceTypePolicy" that grants permissions for the actions organizations:DisableAWSServiceAccess, organizations:EnableAWSServiceAccess, and organizations:ListAWSServiceAccessForOrganization on all resources. Finally, the template should output the ARN of the created execution role.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure and highly available VPC network infrastructure spanning two Availability Zones, with two public subnets and two private subnets, along with an Internet Gateway, two NAT Gateways (one in each public subnet), and associated route tables to direct traffic: public subnets route to the Internet Gateway via a default route 0.0.0.0/0, while private subnets route to their respective NAT Gateways for outbound internet access. The template should accept parameters for the VPC CIDR (default 10.0.0.0/16), and the CIDR blocks for each subnet: PublicSubnetA (10.0.0.0/24), PublicSubnetB (10.0.1.0/24), PrivateSubnetA (10.0.2.0/24), and PrivateSubnetB (10.0.3.0/24). The subnets should be placed in separate AZs using the region’s availability zones. The NAT Gateways require Elastic IPs that depend on the Internet Gateway attachment. Finally, export the VPC ID and each subnet ID with the names Basic-VPC, Basic-PublicSubnetA, Basic-PublicSubnetB, Basic-PrivateSubnetA, and Basic-PrivateSubnetB for cross-stack references.

Specifically, create an empty layer named "test-gracefull-exit" with no requirements or inline code; a layer named "boto3-latest" that includes the boto3 package; a layer named "requests-latest" that includes the requests package; a layer named "pydantic-latest" that includes the pydantic package, noting that pydantic has a compiled pydantic-core dependency so the builder's architecture must match the consumer function's architecture (x86_64 builder for x86_64 consumer); a layer named "inline-code-only" that contains no pip packages but includes a file named "eratosthenes.py" with base64-encoded Python code implementing the Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm; a layer named "inline-code-and-requirements" that includes the python-whois package and a file named "module.py" with base64-encoded code that imports whois and defines an examine function; and an arm64 variant of the boto3 layer named "boto3-latest-arm64" using the arm64 ServiceToken import so that C extensions are built natively for Graviton consumer functions. Additionally, create an IAM role named LambdaExecutionRole that allows the Lambda service to assume it and grants permissions to create log groups, log streams, and put log events in CloudWatch Logs. Finally, create a Lambda function named DemoLambdaFuntion (note the intentional typo) with runtime python3.14, a 60-second timeout, and an inline code handler that imports boto3, pydantic, requests, the examine function from lambdalayer.module, and the sieve function from lambdalayer.eratosthenes, then prints their versions and test outputs. The function must be attached to the LambdaExecutionRole and include all five layers: Boto3LambdaLayer, RequestsLambdaLayer, PydanticLambdaLayer, InlineCodeWithPipPackageLambdaLayer, and InlineCodeLambdaLayer.

The template should accept three parameters: the Lambda function name defaulting to "MyLambdaFunction", the runtime environment defaulting to python3.9 with allowed values including python3.8, python3.9, nodejs16.x, and nodejs18.x, and the handler defaulting to "index.handler". It must create a dedicated IAM role with a name matching "<function-name>-execution-role" that allows the lambda.amazonaws.com service to assume the role and grants permission to create CloudWatch log groups, log streams, and put log events. The Lambda function itself should use inline Python code that returns a simple 200 status code response with the body "Hello from Lambda!", and its execution role must reference the IAM role ARN via the GetAtt intrinsic function. Finally, the template should output the name of the created Lambda function for downstream reference.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel, along with optional HLS and DASH origin endpoints, and optionally a VOD workflow with a packaging group, packaging configurations, and assets, based on the provided S3 bucket names. The template should accept parameters for the archive bucket (for live-to-VOD), the manifest name (defaulting to "index"), the output type (choose from APPLE_HLS, ISO_DASH, or ALL, defaulting to APPLE_HLS), startover window in seconds (default 0), segment duration in seconds (default 3), and a VOD source bucket (if provided, the VOD workflow is created). Additional parameters include a logical name prefix (default "MediaPackage"), environment (default "production"), and custom tags (default key "createdby" and value "aws-cloudformation-templates"). The template must create an IAM role for MediaPackage to assume, with policies granting read access to the VOD source bucket (if provided), write access to the archive bucket (if provided), and full access to SecretsManager for secrets retrieval and role pass/read. The MediaPackage channel is always created. For HLS and DASH endpoints, conditionally create them based on the output type: if the output type is APPLE_HLS or ALL, create an HLS endpoint; if ISO_DASH or ALL, create a DASH endpoint. The origination for endpoints should be DENY if a live-to-VOD archive bucket is provided, otherwise ALLOW. For VOD workflows, if a VOD source bucket is provided, create a packaging group, and conditionally create HLS and DASH packaging configurations and assets based on the output type. The role name should follow the pattern {LogicalName}-MediaPackage-{Region}. Outputs should include the channel ID, the HLS endpoint URL (if created), the DASH endpoint URL (if created), and the manifest name. All resources should be tagged with the environment and custom tag key-value pair.

The template must include an IAM OIDC provider configured with the URL https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, a client ID list containing sts.amazonaws.com, and the thumbprint 6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1. The role must include a deny policy named OidcSafetyPolicy that blocks the sts:AssumeRole action on all resources, and an allow policy named GitHubActionsDeployPolicy that grants s3:PutObject permission specifically on the bucket ghu2023-demo and all objects within it.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an EC2 Image Builder pipeline to produce both x86 and ARM64 Amazon Linux 2023 golden AMIs pre-configured with Docker, Docker Compose, Git, Python 3, and the Synapse client with pandas and pysftp dependencies, intended for use by a research team that requires a standardized, publicly shareable base image. The template should accept parameters for the AWS Organizations ID (defaulting to "o-69lcdj4kro") to share the AMI with the entire organization, an image version string (defaulting to "0.0.0"), and a configurable EBS volume size between 8 and 500 GB (defaulting to 32 GB). It must create an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder managed policies, attached to an instance profile under the path /executionServiceEC2Role/, and an infrastructure configuration referencing that profile. A single component should be defined for Linux platforms supporting Amazon Linux 2023 that installs Docker and Docker Compose via dnf, adds the ec2-user and ssm-user to the docker group, grants ssm-user passwordless sudo access, and includes a test phase that validates Docker Compose, Python imports, and sudoers syntax. Two image recipes must be created, one for x86 and one for ARM64, each using the respective latest Amazon Linux 2023 parent image ARN, including the AWS update-linux and amazon-cloudwatch-agent-linux components plus the custom component, with a root block device mapping at /dev/xvda using the specified volume size and encryption set to false for public sharing, and a base64-encoded user data override that runs dnf upgrade and pip3 upgrades for the Synapse client on boot. A distribution configuration should distribute the AMI only to the current region, tagging the AMI with the stack name, granting launch permission to the specified organization ARN, and making the AMI globally public by including the "all" user group. Finally, two Image resources must be created, one for each architecture, referencing the respective recipe, the infrastructure configuration, and the distribution configuration, with appropriate name tags.

cfn_description: svcrolegen-AWS-Route53-HostedZone-role
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IAM service role specifically designed to allow CloudFormation to manage Route 53 hosted zones on behalf of the user, with the role named AWS-Route53-HostedZone-cfnservicerole. The role must trust the CloudFormation service principal to assume it and should include three separate policies to enforce least-privilege permissions for create, update, and delete operations on hosted zones. The create policy must grant permissions for route53:CreateHostedZone and ec2:DescribeVpcs on all resources, along with route53:ChangeTagsForResource and route53:CreateQueryLoggingConfig scoped to any hosted zone, and route53:GetChange scoped to any change resource. The update policy should allow route53:UpdateHostedZoneComment, route53:AssociateVPCWithHostedZone, and route53:DisassociateVPCFromHostedZone on hosted zones, plus route53:DeleteQueryLoggingConfig on query logging configurations. The delete policy must permit route53:DeleteHostedZone and route53:ListQueryLoggingConfigs on hosted zones, and route53:DeleteQueryLoggingConfig on query logging configurations. The role path should be set to "/" and the role name must be exactly AWS-Route53-HostedZone-cfnservicerole.

cfn_description: This template creates some Alarms and Scaling Policies to manage an AutoScaling Group
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates CloudWatch alarms and Auto Scaling policies to manage an existing WordPress Auto Scaling group, which is referenced via an imported output value named WordpressAutoscalingGroup. The template should define two scaling policies: one to scale up by increasing capacity by one instance with a cooldown period of one second, and another to scale down by decreasing capacity by one instance with the same cooldown. Additionally, create two CloudWatch alarms on the EC2 CPUUtilization metric, both with an evaluation period of one minute and using the average statistic, tied to the Auto Scaling group via the AutoScalingGroupName dimension. The high CPU alarm should trigger when average CPU utilization exceeds 75 percent, with a threshold comparison of greater than, and it should invoke the scale-up policy as its alarm action. The low CPU alarm should trigger when average CPU utilization falls below 25 percent, using a less-than comparison, and it should invoke the scale-down policy. Both alarms should have descriptive alarm descriptions indicating whether the CPU is too high or too low, and they should be configured with a period of 60 seconds. The template must not create any new Auto Scaling groups or EC2 instances, only the alarms and policies that operate on the imported group.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates IAM roles and instance profiles for a Banzai Cloud Pipeline Kubernetes Engine (PKE) cluster, designed to grant EC2 instances the necessary permissions for both master and worker nodes. The template must define two IAM roles: a WorkerRole and a MasterRole, each with an AssumeRolePolicyDocument allowing the ec2.amazonaws.com service to assume the role. The WorkerRole must be attached to the AWS managed policy AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy and include a custom inline policy named PkeKubernetesWorkerPolicy that grants permissions for EC2 describe operations, ECR authentication and image retrieval, and a comprehensive set of autoscaling actions (including describing, updating, setting desired capacity, terminating instances, and managing lifecycle hooks). The MasterRole requires a custom inline policy named PkeKubernetesMasterPolicy that covers EC2 describe, create, modify, attach, and delete actions for security groups, volumes, routes, tags, and instance attributes; ECR authentication and image operations; and extensive Elastic Load Balancing permissions for both Classic and Application Load Balancers (including creating, deleting, modifying, registering targets, and managing listeners), as well as the iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole action. Both roles must have unique names formed by concatenating the stack name with a hyphen and the suffix "-worker" or "-master" respectively. The template must also create two instance profiles: MasterInstanceProfile and WorkerInstanceProfile, each referencing the corresponding role, with instance profile names composed of the stack name, a hyphen, the role type ("master" or "worker"), and "-profile". Finally, the template should export the following outputs for use by other stacks: the stack name, the MasterInstanceProfile and WorkerInstanceProfile references (exported as `${StackName}-MasterInstanceProfile` and `${StackName}-WorkerInstanceProfile`), the WorkerRole, and the MasterRole (exported as `${StackName}-WorkerRole` and `${StackName}-MasterRole`).

cfn_description: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark Metric Alarms
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of CloudWatch metric filters, alarms, and CloudWatch Logs query definitions to monitor an AWS account against the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, specifically covering sections 3.1 through 3.14, all tied to a single CloudTrail log group. The template should accept two parameters: the ARN for an SNS topic to send alarm notifications, with a default value of 'arn:aws:sns:aws-region:your-account#:your-CIS-Alarms', and the name of the CloudTrail CloudWatch Log Group, with a default value of 'Example-Cloudwatch-For-Trail-LogGroup'. For each of the 14 CIS controls, you must create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that parses the log group for specific patterns, a corresponding CloudWatch alarm that triggers when the sum of that metric over a 300-second period (except for the KMS key alarm which uses a 60-second period) is greater than or equal to a threshold of 1, with missing data treated as not breaching, and a CloudWatch Logs query definition that provides a pre-built query for investigating the events. The specific controls to implement are: 3.1 for unauthorized API calls filtering on error codes '*UnauthorizedOperation' or 'AccessDenied*'; 3.2 for console sign-ins without MFA filtering on 'ConsoleLogin' events where 'MFAUsed' is not 'Yes'; 3.1 and 3.3 combined for root account usage filtering on user identity type 'Root' where 'invokedBy' does not exist and the event type is not 'AwsServiceEvent'; 3.4 for IAM policy changes filtering on a comprehensive list of 16 IAM event names like DeleteGroupPolicy, PutRolePolicy, and AttachUserPolicy; 3.5 for CloudTrail configuration changes filtering on CreateTrail, UpdateTrail, DeleteTrail, StartLogging, and StopLogging; 3.6 for console authentication failures filtering on 'ConsoleLogin' events with an error message of 'Failed authentication'; 3.7 for disabling or scheduled deletion of customer-created CMKs filtering on events from 'kms.amazonaws.com' with event names 'DisableKey' or 'ScheduleKeyDeletion'; 3.8 for S3 bucket policy changes filtering on events from 's3.amazonaws.com' with event names like PutBucketAcl, PutBucketPolicy, and DeleteBucketPolicy; 3.9 for AWS Config configuration changes filtering on events from 'config.amazonaws.com' with event names StopConfigurationRecorder, DeleteDeliveryChannel, PutDeliveryChannel, and PutConfigurationRecorder; 3.10 for security group changes filtering on event names like AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, CreateSecurityGroup, and DeleteSecurityGroup; 3.11 for NACL changes filtering on event names like CreateNetworkAcl, DeleteNetworkAclEntry, and ReplaceNetworkAclAssociation; 3.12 for network gateway changes filtering on event names like CreateCustomerGateway, AttachInternetGateway, and DetachInternetGateway; 3.13 for route table changes filtering on event names like CreateRoute, ReplaceRouteTableAssociation, and DeleteRoute; and 3.14 for VPC changes filtering on event names like CreateVpc, ModifyVpcAttribute, and AcceptVpcPeeringConnection. All alarms must send their notifications to the referenced SNS topic ARN, and the template should include the necessary DependsOn clauses to ensure the alarms are created in the correct order, specifically the RootAccountLoginsAlarm depends on the NoMfaConsoleLoginsAlarm, the FailedConsoleLoginsAlarm depends on the RootAccountLoginsAlarm, and the DisabledOrDeletedCmksAlarm depends on the FailedConsoleLoginsAlarm.

For debugging and analysis, include queries that calculate model efficiency metrics including total, average, minimum, and maximum tokens per request by model and token type, cache hit rate analysis by user and model that computes cache hits versus cache misses and the percentage of cache hits, cache hit rate over time on an hourly basis, cache hits by session, cache misses by session, peak usage windows in 15-minute intervals showing window tokens, requests, and active users, a session deep dive query that filters for a placeholder session ID "SESSION_ID_HERE" and displays all relevant fields chronologically, a metric field explorer that parses and displays all available fields including user email, user ID, session ID, organization, model, token type, terminal type, OTel library, and token count, and a daily usage summary query showing total tokens and requests per day for the last 30 days. user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure, production-ready Terraform S3 state backend, including an S3 bucket for storing state files, a DynamoDB table for state locking, a KMS key for encryption, an IAM role for managing state, and a CloudTrail trail for auditing data events, all designed to avoid the chicken-and-egg problem of needing Terraform to create its own backend. The template should accept a customizable Name parameter that defaults to "terraform-state-AWS_ACCOUNT_ID" for the bucket, table, and role names, and allow configuration of lifecycle rules with a NoncurrentVersionExpirationInDays defaulting to 90 days for purging old state versions. For the logging trail, it must create a separate S3 bucket with configurable LogsArchiveInDays of 30 days to move logs to Glacier and LogsDeleteInDays of 365 days for deletion, with an optional ObjectLockEnabled feature that locks log objects for 30 days in GOVERNANCE mode when LogsObjectLockInDays is set to a non-zero value. The template should include a CloudWatch Logs group (enabled by default via the LogsGroup parameter) for state changes, with a dedicated IAM role for CloudTrail to write logs, and both the log group and trail role should be conditionally created only when LogsGroup is set to Enabled. The KMS key must have key rotation enabled and a policy that allows the root account full management, restricts encrypt/decrypt operations to only via S3 and DynamoDB services, permits CloudTrail to generate data keys, and allows CloudWatch Logs to use the key for encryption. The S3 state bucket must be private, enforce server-side encryption with the KMS key, block all public access, enable versioning, and have a bucket policy that denies PutObject requests that do not use the specific KMS key, and optionally restricts all S3 actions to requests originating from a specific VPC when the StateVpcId parameter is provided. The DynamoDB lock table should use pay-per-request billing, have a single attribute LockID of type String as the hash key, enable point-in-time recovery, contributor insights, and server-side encryption using the KMS key. The IAM role must allow the ExecutionPrincipal (defaulting to the root account) to assume it, with an optional condition requiring the principal to have a tag "Repository" with a value containing the Repository parameter when ExecutionConditionTag is Enabled, and similarly allow the AdminPrincipal to assume the role with an optional tag condition when AdminConditionTag is Enabled, and also support an SSOPermissionSet parameter to allow any role matching the AWSReservedSSO pattern to assume the role. The role should be tagged with the Repository tag and have a policy granting ListBucket and GetObject/PutObject on the state bucket, GetItem/PutItem/DeleteItem on the lock table, and DescribeKey/Encrypt/Decrypt/ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey actions on the KMS key. The CloudTrail trail must log all data events for the state bucket, use the KMS key for encryption, write to the trail bucket, and optionally send logs to the CloudWatch log group. The template should output the KMS key alias and ID, lock table name, log group name, region, role ARN, and state bucket name.

The FisAccessControlNonUser role must explicitly deny all fis:* actions while still allowing service-linked role creation. cfn_description: Builds an ElastiCache Redis Cluster, Security Group, and Route53 CNAME
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ElastiCache Redis cluster along with its associated security group and a Route53 CNAME record, designed for a UAT environment. The template should reference an existing VPC and Route53 private hosted zone through cross-stack imports, using the default stack names "UAT-VPC" and "UAT-Route53" respectively. The nested stack templates should be pulled from an S3 bucket named "dchash2buildbucket" in the ap-southeast-2 region, with the security group template file named "EC2-SecurityGroup-ElastiCacheRedis.yaml", the Redis cluster template file named "ElastiCache-Redis.yaml", and the Route53 record set template file named "Route53-RecordSet.yaml". The Redis cluster should be configurable with a cache node type defaulting to cache.t2.micro, allowing selection from t2 and m4 instance families, a number of cache clusters between 1 and 3 defaulting to 1, a port defaulting to 6379, and a maintenance window defaulting to "Sun:05:00-Sun:07:00". The template must support high availability by enabling auto-failover when more than one cache cluster is specified, and the cluster should be placed in the private subnets imported from the VPC stack (PrivateSubnetA, PrivateSubnetB, PrivateSubnetC). The security group should be created within the imported VPC and passed to the Redis cluster. The Route53 record should be a CNAME type with a TTL of 300 seconds, using the hostname "DCHash2redis" and the private domain name imported from the Route53 stack, pointing to the Redis cluster's connection endpoint. All resources must be tagged with environment (defaulting to UAT, with options for Production or Test), business unit (defaulting to Gaming, with options for Charitable, Corporate, Lotteries, or Wagering), department (defaulting to BrandName), application (defaulting to SomePlatform), and component (defaulting to ElastiCache-Redis). The template should export the cache connection address and security group ID as stack outputs for use by other stacks.

cfn_description: Deploy a service into an ECS cluster behind a private load balancer.
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS service running an nginx container behind a private Application Load Balancer, designed to be deployed as part of a larger parent cluster stack named "production" which provides the cluster name, VPC ID, and private listener ARN via cross-stack exports. The template should accept parameters for the service name (defaulting to nginx), the Docker image URL (defaulting to nginx), the container port (defaulting to 80), CPU units (defaulting to 256), memory in megabytes (defaulting to 512), a path pattern for routing traffic (defaulting to "*" to catch all paths), a priority for the listener rule (defaulting to 1), the desired number of running tasks (defaulting to 2), and an optional IAM role ARN for the task if the container needs access to other AWS resources. The template must conditionally assign the task role only when a custom role is provided. It should create an ECS task definition with the specified CPU, memory, and container port mapping, an ECS service that runs the desired count of tasks with a deployment configuration allowing up to 200% during deployments and maintaining at least 75% healthy instances, an Application Load Balancer target group on port 80 with HTTP health checks every 6 seconds, a 5-second timeout, 2 healthy and 2 unhealthy thresholds, and a listener rule on the imported private listener that forwards traffic matching the specified path pattern to the target group with the given priority. The service must depend on the listener rule to ensure proper ordering. All resources should use the service name as the family name for the task definition and the target group name.
